title: Addressing Challenges Faced by Caregivers of Children with Special Needs
what_it_is: Addressing Challenges Faced by Caregivers of Children with Special Needs

sections.label: Lien Foundation special needs survey
sections.summary: A Lien Foundation survey found 28% agreed Singapore is inclusive for special needs children, 71% of parents supported inclusive education, 58% were comfortable with their child in the same school, and 32% of the public believed typically developing children are comfortable interacting with special needs children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The Lien Foundation survey, results of which were published in the media last week on 4 July 2016, revealed, among others, the following results in its poll of the general public and parents of children with special needs: only Page: 64 28% of those surveyed agreed that Singapore is an inclusive society when it comes to special needs children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Whilst a great majority of parents surveyed, about 71%, supported inclusive education, only slightly more than half, 58%, will be comfortable with their child attending the same school as a child with special needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Only 32% of the general public polled believed that typically developing children are comfortable interacting with children of special needs.

sections.label: Kindergarten teacher response to mother
sections.summary: A mother said teachers typically recommended her child be enrolled in a special needs school, as the kindergarten has no allied professionals to help in such situations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I asked the mother whether she had brought this matter up to the attention of teachers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: She informed me that the typical response of the teachers – as the kindergarten does not have any allied professionals to help in such situations – would be to recommend that her child be enrolled in a special needs school instead.

sections.label: Day Activity Centres waiting time
sections.summary: The waiting time for a place in one of the three Day Activity Centres for Autistic Adults stands at two years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I do not propose to repeat what has already been said.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I do, however, wish to update the House that the waiting time to get a place in one of the three Day Activity Centres for Autistic Adults stands at two years.

sections.label: Grants and employability for special needs
sections.summary: The speaker proposed caregivers of adult children with moderate to severe special needs receive the same grants and concessions as other caregivers for foreign domestic maids, and more funding for models enhancing employability within Day Activity Centres, such as horticultural or cafeteria arenas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Also, the special needs children with moderate to severe forms of disabilities may unlearn what they have learnt in school.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I further propose that caregivers of adult children with moderate to severe forms of special needs be given the same form of grants and concessions that caregivers of disabled or the elderly or the young enjoy with respect to employment of foreign domestic maids.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This will, hopefully, give the caregivers some level of respite.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I would also advocate that the Government look at providing more funding support to encourage the adoption of models that would enhance the employability of adult children with special needs within the Day Activity Centres; for example, in the horticultural or cafeteria arenas.

sections.label: Autism lifetime cost study
sections.summary: A study published in The Economist on 16 April 2016 found the lifetime cost of supporting an autistic American is much lesser than the opportunity cost of lost output when autistic people are jobless or underemployed or caregivers leave jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: A study by researchers from the University of California and Old Dominion University published in a seminal article on autism appearing in The Economist on 16 April 2016 reveals that the lifetime cost of supporting an autistic American is much lesser than the opportunity cost, referring to an estimate of the output lost when autistic people are jobless or underemployed or when their caregivers leave their jobs to take care of them.

sections.label: We are Able and See the True Me
sections.summary: The "We are Able" campaign and the "See the True Me" campaign by NCSS were recently launched.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: Recently, we launched a campaign called the "We are Able" campaign and the "See the True Me" campaign by NCSS.

sections.label: Support for special needs children
sections.summary: Over 20,000 children with special needs attend mainstream MOE schools and are supported in various ways.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: A second theme is really about providing support to special needs children in mainstream schools.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: There are over 20,000 children with special needs attending mainstream MOE schools and these children are supported in various ways.

sections.label: Post-18 options for SPED graduates
sections.summary: MOE, MSF and SG Enable started the School-to-Work programme to provide more work and training options for these students.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: We are very aware of their concerns regarding the limited options that 	persons with disabilities have after graduating from SPED schools.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: We are currently studying the opportunities to increase the post-18 range of options.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: MOE, MSF and SG Enable have started the School-to-Work (S2W) programme, which involves the schools, employers and parents to provide more work and training options for these students.

sections.label: PSEA extension for SPED graduates
sections.summary: The Ministry has been working with MOE to extend the Post-Secondary Education Account to special needs children after SPED graduation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: My Ministry has been working with MOE for the Post-Secondary Education Account (PSEA) to be extended to special needs children following their graduation from SPED for skills development and further training to enhance their work capability.

sections.label: Day care places for autism
sections.summary: The Ministry is on track to add 200 more day care places by 2018 for Day Activity Centres catering to persons with autism.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: Our Ministry will be expanding the range of home and community care options to meet the needs of the various groups.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: We are currently on track to add 200 more day care places by 2018 for Day Activity Centres specifically catering to persons with autism.

sections.label: Subsidies for care services
sections.summary: Caregivers accessing care services receive means-tested subsidies that can defray up to 80% of their costs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: In terms of subsidies for care services and transportation, caregivers who are accessing care services, such as Day Activity Centres, Home-based care services and the Drop-in Disability Programme, it is also important for us to support the effort to get there.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: So, they receive continued support from the Government through means-tested subsidies which can defray up to 80% of their costs.

sections.label: Transport subsidies for persons with disabilities
sections.summary: Eligible persons with disabilities may receive transport subsidies of up to 80% of their monthly transport fares.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: Eligible	persons with disabilities may receive transport subsidies of up to 80% of their monthly transport fares.

sections.label: FDW levy and grant support
sections.summary: Caregivers needing foreign domestic workers for persons with disabilities pay a lower monthly levy, and families with monthly per capita income under $2,600 get a monthly FDW Grant.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: Caregivers who require the assistance of foreign domestic workers (FDWs) to care for 	persons with disabilities with their activities of daily living are eligible to pay a lower monthly FDW levy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: Families whose monthly per capita income is less than $2,600 are supported through a monthly FDW Grant to offset the cost of a foreign domestic worker.

sections.label: Special needs trust and savings
sections.summary: The Special Needs Trust Company was set up in 2008 for trust management, and the Special Needs Savings Scheme in 2012 lets parents set aside CPF savings for children with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: To address this concern, the Special Needs Trust Company (SNTC) was set up in 2008 to provide trust management services for families of 	persons with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: Along with SNTC, we set up the Special Needs Savings Scheme which was established in 2012 to enable parents to set aside CPF savings for the long-term care of their Children with Disabilities.
